result.summary: Inlines and optimizes `CBlockIndexWorkComparator` and `arith_uint256` comparisons by defining them in headers using `std::tie`, `noexcept`, and C++20 `operator<=>`. Replaces the out-of-line `base_uint::CompareTo` call with a direct three-way comparison loop. Adds a dedicated benchmark along with unit tests and differential fuzz targets verifying equivalence with previous comparison logic.
result.problem: Block index candidate sorting and chainstate traversal functions (like `CheckBlockIndex` and `FindMostWorkChain`) call `CBlockIndexWorkComparator` heavily. The comparator and its underlying `arith_uint256` work comparison were defined out-of-line with manual branch cascades, preventing the compiler from inlining and optimizing hot comparison loops.
evidence: Author's benchmarks show `CBlockIndexWorkComparator` speedup of 6.5x–6.8x (from ~100M cmp/s to 650M–680M cmp/s) across GCC and Clang.
Author's benchmark measurements show `CheckBlockIndex` throughput increasing by 1.39x–1.62x (reducing op time from ~110µs to ~68µs).
result.scope_notes: Modifies core comparison routines in headers (`arith_uint256.h` and `blockstorage.h`); adds two new fuzz targets checking equivalence against original comparison routines.
result.card: This PR optimizes block index comparisons by moving `CBlockIndexWorkComparator` and `arith_uint256` ordering into headers, rewriting them with `std::tie`, `noexcept`, and C++20 `operator<=>`. Profiling in `CheckBlockIndex` and candidate chain searches identified the comparator and out-of-line `base_uint::CompareTo` calls as avoidable overhead in the hot validation path. Microbenchmarks from the author demonstrate a 6.5x to 6.8x speedup in the work comparator and a 1.4x to 1.6x speedup in `CheckBlockIndex`. Equivalence tests and two dedicated fuzz targets ensure ordering behavior remains unchanged. No dependencies are stated.
